subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should browser-origin requests to privileged Gateway plugin HTTP routes be rejected in every authentication mode, including trusted-proxy and intentionally configured no-auth deployments?
rationale: The correct policy for ambient or absent authentication changes the security and reverse-proxy compatibility contract, so it requires an explicit security-owner decision after live reproduction.

options.title: Enforce Shared Origin Checks
options.body: Reject disallowed browser origins at the shared Gateway plugin-route authentication boundary across all supported authentication modes, with upgrade and proxy coverage.

options.title: Restrict Ambient Modes
options.body: Keep bearer-token behavior unchanged but reject browser-origin privileged routes specifically when trusted-proxy or no-auth configuration would otherwise provide ambient authority.

options.title: Document Existing Boundary
options.body: If live testing proves current origin enforcement already blocks the reported request, document the verified deployment requirements and close without code changes.

recommendation.title: Enforce Shared Origin Checks
recommendation.body: Reject disallowed browser origins at the shared Gateway plugin-route authentication boundary across all supported authentication modes, with upgrade and proxy coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their documented Core, Gateway, and security ownership most directly spans the shared authentication boundary requiring a decision.
